title: Choose an invented word by meaning and grammar
observableEvidence: Uses definition, sentence, and part of speech to infer meaning.
prompt: Three invented words: tarvish (adjective) means careless about small details; quorlwise (adjective) means careful about small details; quorlness (noun) means care about small details. Which one fits the blank: "The ___ editor caught every missing comma."? Enter one option exactly: tarvish, quorlwise, or quorlness.
solutionRepresentation: quorlwise. The blank comes before the noun "editor", so it needs an adjective, and catching every missing comma shows care about small details. Tarvish is an adjective with the opposite meaning; quorlness has the right meaning but is a noun.
solutionMethod: Use the sentence to fix both the meaning and the part of speech the blank needs.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Provisional SP-1 ruling C-1: contest mode keeps a legacy text validator whose only accepted answer is the exact option text listed in the prompt. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores trailing punctuation; any other wording is rejected.

hintSteps.prompt: The blank sits right before the word "editor". Think about what kind of word describes a noun.
hintSteps.question: What part of speech does the blank need?

hintSteps.prompt: Now use the rest of the sentence. Catching every missing comma tells you what the editor is like.
hintSteps.question: Which meaning does the sentence support, and which options are the right part of speech?

hintSteps.prompt: Example with different invented words: in "The ___ dog barked all night," an adjective meaning "noisy" fits the blank, but a noun meaning "noise" does not, even though the meanings match.
hintSteps.question: Which option is both the right part of speech and the right meaning here?
